messages.subject: actionButton, equivalent of "onClick"
parts:
Hi,

I'm struggling with actionButton reactions.

Here's what I want to do : I got an app, that lets the user upload a csv file, and then performs analysis on it. All this part it working quiet nicely.

For a better experience, I'm trying to add a "default dataset" button, that, once clicked, would load a local file into the analysis script.

My problem is with reactive value of actionButton.

Here's a sample of my code :

upload <- reactive({
        csvPath <- input$file1 # this is a fileInput UI control)
        if (is.null(csvPath) && input$myActionButton == 0){
            return()
        } else if (is.null(csvPath) && input$myActionButton > 0){
            csvPath <- "data/AuPop_full.csv" # a locally stored CSV
        } else {
            csvPath <- csvPath$datapath
        }
        baseData <- read.csv(file=csvPath,
                             quote=input$quote,
                             sep=input$sep,
                             header=input$header,
                             check.names = FALSE)
       
        allColumns <- c("None", unlist(colnames(baseData)))
        if (csvPath == "data/AuPop_full.csv"){
            testDataUpdateInputs(session, allColumns)
        } else {
            updateInputs(session, allColumns)
        }
        return(baseData)  
    })


Here's the trouble i'm experiencing :

Depending on the way I create the actionButton reactive test (the chain of if/else), some awaited behavior doesn't work :

1) I don't want the test dataset to be loaded by default (on startup), so, I need a condition like input$myActionButton > 0

2) When doing so, I still want the user to be able to load his own dataset, even after playing with the test dataset. So, a simple input$myActionButton > 0 will always be true once the actionButton is pressed, and so, the condition will always be true, and thus, it will always load the test dataset when the user chooses his own file.

3) The other solution would be to first check for input$file1, and then, for myActionButton. But then, once a personnal dataset is loaded, the user won't be able to load the test dataset once again.

I must confess I have absolutely no idea of how I could solve this problem.
A simple "onClick" action, like in javascript, would be way much easier for me to understand in such situation.

Any idea how I could get the results I want ?

Thanks for your help


Robin

messages.subject: Re: actionButton, equivalent of "onClick"
parts:
For once, side effects are needed! With the code below, the dataset() reactive will return either NULL (on startup), the example dataset, or the uploaded file.

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  values <- reactiveValues(mode = 'none')

  observe({
    if (input$myActionButton > 0) {
      values$mode <- 'example'
    }
  })

  observe({
    if (!is.null(input$file1)) {
      values$mode <- 'file'
    }
  })

  dataset <- reactive({
    switch(values$mode,
      none = NULL,
      example = exampleDataset,
      file = {
        read.csv(input$file1$datapath) # ... and whatnot
      }
    )
  })
})

parts: Yes--if you find yourself creating/updating non-reactive global values from a reactive expression or render function or observer, that is a bad code smell!
